Attendance and participation at the City of La Verne Planning Commission meetings are welcomed and
appreciated. Community engagement provides the Planning Commission with valuable information. Regular
Meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month. In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any
person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should
contact the City Clerk’s Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

The Community Center will be open to the public at 6:00 p.m. Materials related to an item on this agenda,
submitted to the Planning Commission after distribution of the agenda packet, are available for public inspection
at the meeting or in the Community Development Department during normal business hours.

Agenda Report
DATE:  May 8, 2024

TO:  Planning Commission

FROM:  Candice Bowcock, Principal Planner

SUBJECT:  Capital Improvement Plan for 2024/25 and 2025/26-2029/30

SUMMARY
The City of La Verne continues to prepare and adopt a Capital Improvement Plan as a
part of the annual budget and to more responsibly plan for long range capital
improvements. A comprehensive Capital Improvement Plan such as this requires, per
State law, review by the Planning Commission for consistency with the adopted General
Plan. The proposed next fiscal year (2024/25) and five-year (2025/26-2029/30) Capital
Improvement Plan lists all capital improvements and special projects to be undertaken.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends the Planning Commission review the proposed Capital Improvement
Plan, and adopt Resolution No. 1325, certifying that the proposed Capital Improvement
Plan, for year (2024/25) and five-year (2025/26-2029/30), is consistent with the adopted
General Plan.

DISCUSSION
The proposed Capital Improvement Projects include 54 projects for year 2024/25 and
24 for the five-year program. Given that a number of these projects are dependent upon
grants and other outside resources, full implementation of the program will be
dependent upon available funding. The plan, however, provides a focus and priority for
assessing the viability of projects. The Capital Improvement Plan includes
representation from all City departments, with coordination by the City Manager and
Public Works Director.

The Planning Commission is asked to review the proposed Capital Improvement
Projects and to determine consistency with the adopted General Plan. The Commission
is requested to not attempt to determine the need, cost, or specific description of
individual projects, noting these are determined by the respective departments and City
Manager and will ultimately be approved or rejected by the City Council as part of the
budget adoption process.

Following are tables listing the proposed Capital Improvement Projects and respective
identified General Plan policies. In some cases there are multiple policies identified. It
may also be possible to identify additional policies beyond those shown. The main

   RESOLUTION NO. 1325

A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF LA VERNE,
CALIFORNIA, CERTIFYING THAT THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM FOR FISCAL
YEARS 2024/25 AND 2025/26-2029/30 ARE CONSISTENT WITH THE ADOPTED
GENERAL PLAN.

  THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF LA VERNE DOES HEREBY
RESOLVE AS FOLLOWS:

  WHEREAS, Section 2.48.160 of the La Verne Municipal Code requires the
Commission to take responsibility for the preparation and regular review of the
comprehensive General Plan as provided by California Government Code, Sec. 65300 et
seq.; and

  WHEREAS, the statutory case record demonstrates that capital facility decisions must
be consistent with the General Plan in the same manner that private development projects
must be (Friends Of “B Street v. City of Hayward (1980) 106 Cal.App. 3d 988); and

  WHEREAS, Government Code Sections 53090 et seq. requires that most public
works projects be consistent with zoning and therefore with the General Plan, as provided by
Government Code Section 53096; and

  WHEREAS, the Community Development Department staff have reviewed the
proposed projects and found them conforming to the General Plan; and

  WHEREAS, the PLANNING COMMISSION did consider said capital improvement
request, attached hereto and incorporated by reference, at its meeting on May 8, 2024.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Planning Commission of the City of La
Verne:

  Section 1. The Planning Commission HEREBY FINDS AND DETERMINES that the
capital improvement program is consistent with the goals, objectives, and priorities set forth in
the comprehensive General Plan adopted December 7, 1998.

  Section 2. The Planning Commission HEREBY DIRECTS the Community
Development staff to forward its findings to the City Manager and City Council for
consideration as part of the budget hearing process.

PASSED, APPROVED AND ADOPTED this 8th day of May, 2024, by the Planning
Commission at La Verne, California.

  Chairperson, Planning Commission
